updates.title: Sales and Advisor Analysis reports drop a voided invoice and keep its re-invoice
preconditions: You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission and can create and invoice work orders.

Location {Location-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Quiet 14 Oct A) is a fresh location made for this run: nothing else is invoiced, credited or clocked there, so on the Dashboard the Revenue tile on This Week reads $0.00 with 0 Invoices.
Labor rate {Rate-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST Rate 100) charges $100.00 an hour at {Location-A}.
Customer {Customer-A} (for example ZZAUTOTEST C88632 Void Reinvoice) has one contact and one asset (for example unit ZZ-101).
{User-A} has Time Clock on and is the technician on the work.
Work order {Work-order-1} (for example S490-1201) for {Customer-A} is invoiced, not sent and not paid, and its Service Advisor is {User-A}.

{Work-order-1} has one labor line, {Line-1} (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Line 1"), with technician {User-A}, labor rate {Rate-A}, Estimated Time 2.00 and Tech Time 2.00, and exactly 2.00 hours clocked on it.
You have written down the invoice's Subtotal (for example $200.00).
You run the whole case on one day, and not on the last evening of the week, so every record stays inside This Week.
You can open the release notes page on Confluence (https://shopview.atlassian.net/wiki/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=931069964).
steps: Click Reports in the top menu, then Sales in the left menu.
Set the Date control to This week.
Write down the row for {Work-order-1}'s invoice and the Subtotal in the Totals row.
Click Advisor Analysis in the left menu (the page is titled Service Advisor Analysis) and set the Date control to This week, with no advisor chosen.
Write down the invoice's row: Hrs Worked, Hrs Invoiced, Billing Efficiency, ELR and Subtotal.
Click Work Orders in the top menu and open {Work-order-1}.

On the Lines tab click New Line and add a second line: What Are You Doing? (for example "ZZAUTOTEST Line 2"), Add Technician {User-A}, Labor Rate {Rate-A}, Estimated Time 1.00, Tech Time 1.00, tick Line Approved, then click Save & Close.
On the new line click Story, type a short story and click Update.
Click Complete on the new line (if a window offers Complete All Lines or asks for Mileage, finish it there), then click Mark Reviewed.
Click the Finance tab and write down how it shows the first invoice.
Click Create Invoice, close the New Customer Payment window without paying, and write down the new Subtotal.
Open Reports > Sales again (Date: This week) and write down the rows and the Totals row Subtotal.
Open Reports > Advisor Analysis again (Date: This week, no advisor chosen) and write down the rows and the Totals row.
Click Parts > Part Sales > New Part Sale and try to invoice the sale without choosing a customer. If the screen insists on a customer, stop this step.
Open the release notes page and find the Dashboard note that starts "Sales report totals can change".
results: Steps 3 and 5: Before the void, the Sales report lists the invoice and its Totals row Subtotal is the amount you wrote down (for example $200.00). Advisor Analysis shows Hrs Worked 2.00, Hrs Invoiced 2.00 and Billing Efficiency 100.00% (2.00 / 2.00 x 100).

Steps 10 and 11: Write down how the Finance tab marks the first invoice (for example a Void label) and the new Subtotal (for example $300.00 = $200.00 + 1.00 hour x $100.00). These two readings are records, not pass or fail points.

Step 12: The Sales report lists only the new invoice: the voided invoice is gone, and the Totals row Subtotal equals the new Subtotal (for example $300.00), not the two added together (for example $500.00 = $200.00 + $300.00).

Step 13: Advisor Analysis shows one row for {Work-order-1}, the new invoice, with Hrs Invoiced 3.00 (2.00 + 1.00) and the new Subtotal (for example $300.00). Hrs Worked stays 2.00, so Billing Efficiency reads 150.00% (3.00 / 2.00 x 100). The figures moved up: this is the void-then-reinvoice case.

Step 14: If you could invoice a sale with no customer, it appears in the Sales report total and in Advisor Analysis. If the screen insisted on a customer, write "no-customer invoice not reachable by hand" in the result comment.

Step 15: The note says Sales report totals can change for some past dates: voided invoices are no longer counted, which lowers a total; invoices with no customer attached are now included, which raises one; and a voided invoice that was invoiced again counts only the new amount. It also says the Service Advisor Analysis report changes the same way and walk-in sales now count toward advisor figures. This checks the published notes, not the product screens.

quotes: S3-E2

A voided invoice is excluded from every figure the dashboard shows. It contributes nothing to Revenue or to the parts-versus-labor split, nothing to invoiced hours or invoiced technician hours, and it is counted in neither the Sales by Customer count nor the At Risk Customers count, including when deciding a customer's most recent invoice. This is not a dashboard rule of its own: it is what the reports do, and the dashboard matches them (S3-R1). A void means the document was undone, so a figure that still carried its money or its hours would overstate the shop.
S3-E2 context note (Sales report)

That is a defect in the Sales report rather than a dashboard decision, and it is corrected inside this project so Revenue can match it (@chris ruling, 2026-09-15). Correcting it moves the Sales report's own existing totals for any range containing voided or no-company invoices, so it ships with a release note.
S3-E2 context note (Service Advisor Analysis)

Service Advisor Analysis is a direct copy of the Sales report's invoice query and carries both flaws, so it is corrected in this project too (@chris ruling, 2026-09-16: the figures need to match each other and to be right, and today they are neither). That moves advisor revenue and ELR down for periods containing voided invoices and adds walk-in sales to advisor figures, under the same release note.
Tech plan NFR-010

Both report corrections ship with one plain-language release note: Sales report totals move for ranges containing voided or no-company invoices, and on Service Advisor Analysis revenue, ELR *and the hours columns, and therefore Labor Efficiency %* move for those periods, while advisor figures gain walk-in sales. It must also call out the void-then-reinvoice case, where a figure can move *up*
Release notes, Dashboard, Worth knowing (Confluence 931069964 v7 and 928121200 v6, 14 Oct 2026)

Sales report totals can change for some past dates. Voided invoices are no longer counted, which lowers a total, and invoices with no customer attached are now included, which raises one. A voided invoice that was invoiced again counts only the new amount. The Service Advisor Analysis report changes the same way, and walk-in sales now count toward advisor figures. Expect questions about this.

preconditions: You are signed in as {User-A} (for example Admin ShopView), whose role has the Reports permission, at location {Location-A} (for example Staging Heavy Duty - 9919).
Your browser window is at least 1024 pixels wide at 100% zoom (a maximised laptop or desktop window).
{Location-A} has invoices spread over the last twelve months, so the Revenue tile shows an amount above $0.00 on Last 12 Months.
This month, at least two days at {Location-A} have clocked time on invoiced work, with a day between them that has no clocked time at all, {Day-A} (for example a Sunday).

Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 31 days", and click Apply.
Count the points (corners) on the Revenue trend line.

Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 182 days", and click Apply. Count the points.
Click the Revenue tile's date pill, pick a start day and an end day in the calendar so the readout at the bottom reads "Range: 183 days", and click Apply. Count the points.
Set the Revenue pill to Last 12 Months and click View details on Revenue.
Compare the Revenue trend line's shape with the monthly bars in the Revenue chart.

The 731-day and 732-day ranges were removed because a tile's calendar now allows at most 366 days (S7-R2a, Chris Ward's answer 3 of 14 Oct 2026), so the switch to one point per quarter cannot be reached from a tile. Design canvas board 03_Range_After for the date pill, calendar and "Range: N days" readout. Source-verified 14 October 2026. This version of the case has not yet been checked against a build.
quotes: The sparkline shows the tile's measure trending over the selected range.

The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).
S7-R2a

The control is the same date picker the reports use. Besides the nine presets it offers a calendar for choosing a custom range of up to 366 days, the same limit the reports apply, and a Today button inside the calendar. Today is part of the calendar, not a tenth preset. A custom range is not remembered between visits (S7-R8), and the report opened from the tile shows it as "Custom" (S10-E1).
S6-R3a

The expanded Revenue chart covers the tile's own date range (S7-R5), with one bar per day, week, month or quarter chosen from the length of the range by the same rule as the sparkline (S4-R11). Last 12 Months shows twelve monthly bars; This Month shows daily bars.
S9-R9

In an expanded chart, a month with no value is drawn as a dashed line joining the points on either side of it. This is how these charts already draw in production. A gap in the line applies only to the sparkline on a tile (S4-R11).

quotes: The sparkline draws one point per bucket, and the bucket size is chosen from the length of the selected range: a range of 31 days or fewer buckets by day; 32 to 182 days by week; 183 to 731 days by month; anything longer by quarter. Each point is the measure recomputed over that bucket using the same calculation as the headline, so a point can never disagree with the tile it sits in. A bucket for which the measure has no value (S3-E3) contributes no point, and interior gaps are preserved rather than closed up or drawn as zero. When fewer than two points have values, no line is drawn and the tile shows the empty-chart placeholder instead (S4-R12).
S3-R1

Every figure the dashboard shows for a measure equals the figure the measure's matching report shows for the same workplace, date range, and filters. This holds at every moment, not merely in principle. The dashboard may serve a figure from a cache, but only in a way that cannot produce a difference: the tile and its report must resolve to the same stored calculation, or the cache must be invalidated by the same events that change the report's answer. A tile that shows a different number from its report because one of them is more recently computed than the other is a defect, not an accepted staleness window. There is no freshness allowance and no "up to N minutes behind" in this spec.
A tile shows the empty-chart placeholder in place of its sparkline when fewer than two points in the selected range have a value.
The placeholder is an outline drawn as a light grey dashed line, with rounded corners and no fill. The tile's background shows through it.
A line-chart icon, in grey, sits at the center of the placeholder.
The placeholder changes nothing else on the tile. The headline and the supporting line show their usual values.
S7-R2a

The control is the same date picker the reports use. Besides the nine presets it offers a calendar for choosing a custom range of up to 366 days, the same limit the reports apply, and a Today button inside the calendar. Today is part of the calendar, not a tenth preset. A custom range is not remembered between visits (S7-R8), and the report opened from the tile shows it as "Custom" (S10-E1).
